I couldn't find this in the provided FastAPI docs. The excerpts cover changing where the docs' JavaScript and CSS files come from, such as a different CDN or self-hosted static files. They don't cover running an app behind a reverse proxy like Nginx under a path prefix such as `/api`.

In the FastAPI documentation, look for the **"Behind a Proxy"** guide in the Advanced User Guide, and search for **`root_path`**. That section explains how to make the docs work when your app is served under a prefix.

If the page loads but stays blank because the Swagger UI or ReDoc assets fail to load, a different guide may help. Your network may be blocking the CDN. In that case, the provided docs describe self-hosting those files. The API docs use **Swagger UI** and **ReDoc**, and each of those need some JavaScript and CSS files. By default, those files are served from a CDN.[3] Self-hosting the JavaScript and CSS could be useful if, for example, you need your app to keep working even while offline, without open Internet access, or in a local network.[4]
